open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input representation
open_points.text: Inputs: One JSON value. / Errors: refused for a value JCS cannot represent: a non-finite number, a duplicate key.
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text that can preserve duplicate members, or an already-parsed JSON value in which duplicate keys have been lost, and which layer detects duplicates?
options: Receive raw JSON bytes/text and parse while detecting duplicate keys
Receive a parsed value and require surface's parser to detect duplicate keys before this operation
open_points.default_guess: Receive raw JSON bytes at the surface boundary, reject duplicate keys there, and let internal callers pass parsed values that cannot contain duplicates.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.fit_port_value value size
open_points.text: a JSON value, checked against the port's schema, its size bound applying to the whole value
open_points.question: Which bytes determine the size of a JSON value: the received JSON representation, its RFC 8785 canonical bytes, or another encoding?
options: RFC 8785 canonical-byte length
Original received-byte length
Runtime representation size
open_points.default_guess: Use the length of the RFC 8785 canonical bytes.

open_points.subject: authored TrialCase input and expected-output shape
open_points.text: Inputs: A contract version, input values by port, optional expected outputs
open_points.question: Must inputs contain exactly every contract input and no extras, and when expected outputs are present must they contain exactly every output, or may expected outputs be partial assertions?
options: Inputs must be exact; expected outputs are either absent or exact
Inputs must be exact; expected outputs may name a subset
Both inputs and expected outputs may be partial
open_points.default_guess: Require exact inputs and, when expected outputs are present, exact outputs.

open_points.subject: manifest_source revision semantics
open_points.text: Return the manifest location and revision fixed at start. / The kernel reads a service's record only from <manifest_location>/<service_id>.json at the configured manifest_revision.
open_points.question: How does the configured revision select the bytes read from manifest_location, and what proves that the file belongs to that revision?
options: The kernel reads a version-control repository at the named revision
manifest_location is already a revision-pinned snapshot and revision is metadata
The revision is interpolated into a revision-specific directory or provider API
open_points.default_guess: Treat manifest_location as a repository and read the exact file content from the configured immutable revision.

open_points.subject: ManifestOperation api_base_url
open_points.text: one that is not an absolute http or https URL with a host counts as none / The URL is the api_base_url without a trailing / followed by the declared path.
open_points.question: Are user information, query, fragment, and an existing base path allowed in api_base_url, and precisely how are trailing slashes and the operation path joined?
options: Allow only scheme, host, optional port, and optional normalized base path; forbid userinfo, query and fragment
Allow every absolute URL with a host and join by literal string concatenation
Allow only an origin with no path, query, fragment or userinfo
open_points.default_guess: Allow an origin plus an optional base path, forbid userinfo/query/fragment, remove one terminal slash, and append the declared path.

open_points.subject: plain-http loopback exception
open_points.text: one whose api_base_url host is a loopback address
open_points.question: Does loopback mean only a literal loopback IP in the URL, or may a hostname qualify after DNS resolution, and which IPv4/IPv6 ranges count?
options: Only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses
Any hostname whose current DNS result is entirely loopback
localhost plus literal loopback addresses
open_points.default_guess: Accept only literal addresses in the standard IPv4 127.0.0.0/8 or IPv6 ::1 loopback ranges.

open_points.subject: HTTP header value wire encoding
open_points.text: required_headers with their manifest values verbatim / its content decoded as UTF-8 ... is the value. A resolved value is added as that header.
open_points.question: How are Unicode manifest and credential header values encoded into HTTP field-value bytes, and are non-ASCII values accepted or refused?
options: Require visible ASCII header values
Encode non-ASCII values as UTF-8 bytes
Permit RFC-defined obs-text with an explicitly fixed byte mapping
open_points.default_guess: Require header values to be valid visible ASCII after the stated whitespace and control checks.

open_points.subject: credential trailing-newline and control validation
open_points.text: its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the value / holds an empty value or a control character
open_points.question: What exactly counts as the one removable trailing newline, and what exact character set counts as a control character?
options: Remove one LF or one CRLF and reject ASCII C0 plus DEL
Remove only one LF and reject Unicode General Category Cc
Trim all trailing CR/LF characters and reject every Unicode control or format character
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one terminal LF or CRLF and reject ASCII C0 characters and DEL.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest validation
open_points.text: an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service
open_points.question: A08 rule 5 contains operation-specific checks, but check_installed_instances receives no operation name and runs before the store is opened; which capabilities in the service record are validated, in what order, and which A08 checks count as checks of the record itself here?
options: Validate only service-level structure needed to locate the selected instance and its required headers
Validate every capability in capability-list order
Validate every capability in operation-name code-point order
open_points.default_guess: Validate only service-level structure and the selected instance facts needed for the credential-header collision check.

open_points.subject: effects.decide_effect_approval refusal trace
open_points.text: Inputs: An approval identity, approve or refuse, the actor (the owner); from runs that the run has not ended. / Outputs: The approval approved, or refused with the element's NodeExecution refused_by_owner.
open_points.question: When refusing, where does effects obtain the exact StoredValue and SpooledFile input references required by the new NodeExecution, since EffectApproval specifies input digests and a preview but not an unambiguous set of those references?
options: EffectApproval durably stores the exact input references
runs passes the exact input references to decide_effect_approval
effects reconstructs them from the run and trace
open_points.default_guess: Have runs pass the exact element input references to decide_effect_approval.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile identity and lookup key
open_points.text: Identity: value; equal facts are the same spooled file. / A SpooledFile is named by its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey). / Wherever an answer shows a spooled file ... it carries the SpooledFile's full identity.
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile's identity the complete M22 fact set including digest, size, media type and class, or only its producing-position key, and what exactly must callers preserve as the full identity?
options: Producing position is the identity; content facts are attributes
All M22 facts form the identity, while producing position is only a unique lookup key
Both forms are accepted as identities
open_points.default_guess: Use the producing position as the stable lookup identity and treat digest, size, media type and class as immutable attributes returned with it.

open_points.subject: masked failure_detail length
open_points.text: a failure_detail whose class is above open ... is returned to an agent only as its length and that class
open_points.question: Is the reported length measured in Unicode characters or UTF-8 bytes, and is it the length of the stored, already-bounded failure_detail or of the original untruncated text?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded detail
Unicode code-point length of the stored bounded detail
Length of the original detail before truncation
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, bounded failure_detail.
